plan.estimand: Log-rank test at two-sided alpha 0.05 with hazard ratio 0.7
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test using Freedman approximation
scientific_notes: Freedman approximation uses event probabilities and hazard ratio to compute the asymptotic variance and non-centrality parameter
powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default implements this for survival comparison with censoring implicit in the event probability specification
Calculation will be verified against direct package execution

answer.summary: Power for a two-sided log-rank test comparing survival curves under the Freedman approximation was calculated using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default with 200 participants per group (400 total), hazard ratio 0.7, event probabilities 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), at two-sided alpha 0.05. The achieved power is 0.6383389 (approximately 63.8%).
answer.method: Freedman approximation via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default. The method implements the formula: power = Φ(√(k·m)·|RR−1|/(k·RR+1) − z₁₋ₐ/₂), where m = nE·pE + nC·pC is the total expected number of events, k = nE/nC is the allocation ratio, and z₁₋ₐ/₂ is the critical value from the standard normal distribution. For this design: k=1, m=171.94 total expected events, z₁₋ₐ/₂=1.9599640, noncentrality parameter = 2.3139864.
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test under the Cox proportional-hazards model
Null hypothesis H₀: HR = 1 vs. two-sided alternative H₁: HR ≠ 1
Equal allocation (1:1 ratio) with 200 participants per group
Event probabilities fixed over the study follow-up period: treatment 0.3707, control 0.4890
Asymptotic normality via central limit theorem (large-sample approximation)
limitations: Freedman approximation assumes large samples; validity depends on total event count (171.94 expected events is reasonable but applicability of normal approximation should be verified)
Event probabilities are assumed fixed and known; actual power depends on realized event counts in the trial
Method assumes proportional hazards; substantial departures would affect actual power
No adjustment for multiple comparisons or post-hoc analyses beyond the pre-specified log-rank test

executions.code:
# Load required package
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 200
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
event_prob_treatment <- 0.3707
event_prob_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05
two_sided <- TRUE

# Calculate power using powerCT.default
# powerCT.default expects:
# - n: number of subjects per group (equal allocation)
# - lambda0: event rate in control
# - lambda1: event rate in treatment  
# - rho: hazard ratio (treatment/control)
# - alpha: type I error
# - power: NULL (we want to calculate it)
# - sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided

# From event probabilities, we derive event rates
# The event probability under constant hazard rate is related to the follow-up time
# However, for Freedman's approximation, we can use the event counts directly
# Expected number of events in each group:
n_events_control <- n_per_group * event_prob_control
n_events_treatment <- n_per_group * event_prob_treatment

cat("Study parameters:\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", event_prob_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", event_prob_control, "\n")
cat("Expected number of events (treatment):", n_events_treatment, "\n")
cat("Expected number of events (control):", n_events_control, "\n")
cat("Total expected events:", n_events_treatment + n_events_control, "\n\n")

# powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default uses the Freedman approach
# It requires event rates (lambda) rather than event probabilities
# We interpret the event probabilities as the proportion of participants experiencing the event
# For constant hazard rate: event_prob = 1 - exp(-lambda * tau)
# Solving for lambda: lambda = -log(1 - event_prob) / tau
# But if we set tau = 1 (unit time), then lambda = -log(1 - event_prob)

lambda0 <- -log(1 - event_prob_control)
lambda1 <- -log(1 - event_prob_treatment)

cat("Derived event rates (assuming unit follow-up time):\n")
cat("Control event rate (lambda0):", lambda0, "\n")
cat("Treatment event rate (lambda1):", lambda1, "\n")
cat("Ratio of rates (lambda1/lambda0):", lambda1/lambda0, "\n\n")

# Calculate power using powerCT.default
power_result <- powerCT.default(
  n = n_per_group,
  lambda0 = lambda0,
  lambda1 = lambda1,
  rho = hazard_ratio,
  alpha = alpha,
  power = NULL,
  sided = 2
)

cat("Power calculation via powerCT.default:\n")
cat("Power:", power_result$power, "\n")
cat("Calculation details:\n")
print(power_result)

# Store result for output
power_value <- power_result$power

# Emit structured result
cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Method: Freedman approximation via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default\n")
cat("Power:", power_value, "\n")
cat("Two-sided alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")

_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

      nE: integer. number of participants in the experimental group.

      nC: integer. number of participants in the control group.

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     The power of the test.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     The power formula assumes that the central-limit theorem is valid
     and hence is appropriate for large samples.

     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in
     Medicine_. 1: 121-129

library(powerSurvEpi)

# Study parameters from user request
nE <- 200  # experimental (treatment) group
nC <- 200  # control group
pE <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment
pC <- 0.4890  # event probability in control
RR <- 0.7  # hazard ratio (treatment/control)
alpha <- 0.05  # two-sided, alpha level

# Calculate power using powerCT.default (Freedman approximation)
power <- powerCT.default(
  nE = nE,
  nC = nC,
  pE = pE,
  pC = pC,
  RR = RR,
  alpha = alpha
)

# Display results
cat("=== Freedman Approximation Power Calculation ===\n\n")
cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: Two-sided log-rank test, H0: HR = 1 vs H1: HR ≠ 1\n")
cat("  Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio: 1:1 (equal)\n")
cat("  Sample size per group:", nE, "(treatment) and", nC, "(control)\n")
cat("  Total sample size:", nE + nC, "\n\n")

cat("Effect and Event Parameters:\n")
cat("  Hazard ratio (RR):", RR, "\n")
cat("  Event probability (treatment):", pE, "\n")
cat("  Event probability (control):", pC, "\n")
cat("  Expected events (treatment):", nE * pE, "\n")
cat("  Expected events (control):", nC * pC, "\n")
cat("  Total expected events:", nE * pE + nC * pC, "\n\n")

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("  Power:", power, "\n\n")

cat("Method: Freedman approximation (powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default)\n")
cat("Reference: Freedman (1982), as implemented in Rosner (2006), Section 14.12\n")
cat("The formula used is:\n")
cat("  power = Phi(sqrt(k*m)*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1) - z_{1-alpha/2})\n")
cat("  where m = nE*pE + nC*pC (total expected events)\n")
cat("  and k = nE/nC (allocation ratio)\n")

# Verify calculation manually to show the computation
k <- nE / nC
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC
z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
noncentrality <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(RR - 1) / (k * RR + 1)
power_manual <- pnorm(noncentrality - z_crit)

cat("\n=== Manual Verification ===\n")
cat("k (allocation ratio) = nE/nC:", k, "\n")
cat("m (total expected events) = nE*pE + nC*pC:", m, "\n")
cat("z_{1-alpha/2} (critical value):", z_crit, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter:", noncentrality, "\n")
cat("Power (verified):", power_manual, "\n")

# Emit result for structured reporting
jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(
        metric = "power",
        value = power,
        unit = "probability"
      )
    ),
    method = "logrank_freedman",
    design = list(
      hypothesis = "Two-sided log-rank test, H0: HR=1 vs H1: HR≠1",
      alpha = alpha,
      sidedness = "two-sided",
      allocation_ratio = 1,
      sample_size_treatment = nE,
      sample_size_control = nC,
      total_sample_size = nE + nC,
      hazard_ratio = RR,
      event_probability_treatment = pE,
      event_probability_control = pC,
      total_expected_events = m
    ),
    computation = list(
      k = k,
      m = m,
      z_critical = z_crit,
      noncentrality = noncentrality,
      power_manual_check = power_manual
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

library(powerSurvEpi)

# Study parameters

hazard_ratio <- 0.7
event_prob_treatment <- 0.3707
event_prob_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05
two_sided <- TRUE

# Calculate power using powerCT.default
# powerCT.default expects:
# - n: number of subjects per group (equal allocation)
# - lambda0: event rate in control
# - lambda1: event rate in treatment  
# - rho: hazard ratio (treatment/control)
# - alpha: type I error
# - power: NULL (we want to calculate it)
# - sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided

# From event probabilities, we derive event rates
# The event probability under constant hazard rate is related to the follow-up time
# However, for Freedman's approximation, we can use the event counts directly
# Expected number of events in each group:
n_events_control <- n_per_group * event_prob_control
n_events_treatment <- n_per_group * event_prob_treatment

cat("Study parameters:\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", event_prob_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", event_prob_control, "\n")
cat("Expected number of events (treatment):", n_events_treatment, "\n")
cat("Expected number of events (control):", n_events_control, "\n")
cat("Total expected events:", n_events_treatment + n_events_control, "\n\n")

# powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default uses the Freedman approach
# It requires event rates (lambda) rather than event probabilities
# We interpret the event probabilities as the proportion of participants experiencing the event
# For constant hazard rate: event_prob = 1 - exp(-lambda * tau)
# Solving for lambda: lambda = -log(1 - event_prob) / tau
# But if we set tau = 1 (unit time), then lambda = -log(1 - event_prob)

lambda0 <- -log(1 - event_prob_control)
lambda1 <- -log(1 - event_prob_treatment)

cat("Derived event rates (assuming unit follow-up time):\n")
cat("Control event rate (lambda0):", lambda0, "\n")
cat("Treatment event rate (lambda1):", lambda1, "\n")
cat("Ratio of rates (lambda1/lambda0):", lambda1/lambda0, "\n\n")

# Calculate power using powerCT.default
power_result <- powerCT.default(
  n = n_per_group,
  lambda0 = lambda0,
  lambda1 = lambda1,
  rho = hazard_ratio,
  alpha = alpha,
  power = NULL,
  sided = 2
)

cat("Power calculation via powerCT.default:\n")
cat("Power:", power_result$power, "\n")
cat("Calculation details:\n")
print(power_result)

# Store result for output
power_value <- power_result$power

# Emit structured result
cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Method: Freedman approximation via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default\n")
cat("Power:", power_value, "\n")
cat("Two-sided alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
